exampleAnswers.title: Using Trend Line Equations to Make a Prediction

question.text:
The scatterplot above shows the relationship between the number of hours $x$ a group of people spend watching TV each night and the time $y$ they sleep each night. The equation of the trend line is $y = 10 - 1.25x.$

Assuming this trend continues, estimate the time a person sleeps per night if they watch TV for $6$ hours.
question.explanation:
To predict the number of hours a person sleeps after watching TV for $6$ hours, we need to substitute $x = 6$ into the equation of the trend line: \begin{align*} y & = 10 - 1.25x\\[3pt] & = 10 - 1.25(6)\\[3pt] & = 10 - 7.5\\[3pt] & = 2.5 \end{align*}

Therefore, according to this model, a person watching TV for $6$ hours sleeps for approximately $2.5$ hours.

Note: The point where $x=6$ is not shown on our trend line. Therefore, our result may be unreliable.

question.text:
An ice cream shop wants to determine the relationship between the outside temperature $x$ (in degrees Celsius) and the number of customers $y$ they serve. The scatter plot above shows the information they collected over several days. The equation of the trend line is $y = 2.25x - 19.$

Estimate the outside temperature if they served $53$ customers.
question.explanation:
To predict the outside temperature knowing that they served $53$ customers, we need to substitute $y = 53$ into the equation of the trend line and solve for $x{:}$ \begin{align*} y & = 2.25x - 19\\[3pt] 53 & = 2.25x - 19\\[3pt] 2.25x & = 72\\[3pt] x & = 32 \end{align*}

Therefore, according to this model, the outside temperature is approximately $32^\circ \, \textrm{C}.$

Note: The point where $y=53$ is not shown on our trend line. Therefore, our result may be unreliable.

question.text: The scatter plot above gives the correspondence between the variables $x$ and $y$ for some data points. The equation of the trend line is $y=-0.5x+9.$ Assuming this trend continues, estimate the value of $x$ when $y=2.$
question.explanation:
We can estimate the required value by substituting $y=2$ into the equation of the trend line and solving for $x{:}$

\begin{align*} y &= -0.5x+9 \\[3pt] 2 &= -0.5x+9 \\[3pt] 2+0.5x &= 9 \\[3pt] 0.5x &= 7 \\[3pt] x &=14 \end{align*}

Therefore, according to this model, when $y=2$ we have $x \approx 14.$

Note: The point where $y=2$ is not shown on our trend line. Therefore, our result may be unreliable.

question.explanation:
We can estimate the required value by substituting $x = 10$ into the equation of the trend line:

\begin{align*} y &= 5 - 0.25x \\[3pt] & = 5 - 0.25(10) \\[3pt] & = 5 - 2.5\\[3pt] & = 2.5 \end{align*}

Therefore, according to this model, when $x = 10,$ we have $y \approx 2.5.$

Note: The point where $x=10$ is not shown on our trend line. Therefore, our result may be unreliable.

question.text:
The scatter plot above gives the correspondence between the variables $x$ and $y$ for some data points. Estimate the value of $y$ when $x=20.$

Hint: Assume the trend is linear, and that the trend line passes through the points $(1,23)$ and $(9,27).$
question.explanation:
First, using the hint, let's draw an approximate trend line for our scatter plot.

Our trend line passes through $(x_1,y_1) = (1,23)$ and $(x_2,y_2)=(9,27).$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form \[ y=mx+b. \]

First, we calculate the slope $m$ of the line as follows: \begin{align*} m & = \dfrac {y_2 - y_1} {x_2 - x_1} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{27 - 23}{9 - 1} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{4}{8} \\[5pt] &= 0.5 \end{align*}

Substituting $m = 0.5$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get \[ y = 0.5 x + b. \]

We now need to calculate the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can do this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(1,23)\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} y &= 0.5 x + b \\[3pt] 23 &= 0.5(1) + b \\[3pt] 23 &= 0.5 + b \\[3pt] b &= 22.5 \end{align*}

Therefore, the equation of the line is \[ y = 0.5x + 22.5. \]

Finally, we substitute $x = 20$ into the equation above, which gives \begin{align*} y &= 0.5x + 22.5 \\[3pt] & = 0.5(20) + 22.5 \\[3pt] &= 10 + 22.5 \\[3pt] &= 32.5. \end{align*}

Therefore, according to this model, when $x=20$ we have $y \approx 32.5.$

Note: The point where $x=20$ is not shown on our trend line. Therefore, our result may be unreliable.

question.text:
The scatter plot above shows the relationship between the time (in hours) some college students spend studying the night before an exam and the time they spend sleeping that night. Assuming this trend continues, estimate the time a student spends studying if that student gets only $3.75$ hours of sleep.

Hint: Assume the trend is linear and that the trend line passes through the points $(2,7.5)$ and $(4,5).$
question.explanation:
First, using the hint, let's draw an approximate trend line for our scatter plot.

The trend line passes through $(x_1,y_1) = (2,7.5)$ and $(x_2,y_2) = (4,5).$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form \[ y=mx+b. \]

First, we find the slope $m$ of the line as follows: \begin{align*} m & = \dfrac {y_2 - y_1} {x_2 - x_1} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac {5 - 7.5}{4 - 2} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{(-2.5)}{2} \\[5pt] & = -1.25 \end{align*}

Substituting $m = -1.25$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get \[ y = -1.25x + b. \]

We now need to calculate the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can do this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(4,5)\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} y &= -1.25x + b \\[3pt] 5 &= -1.25(4) + b \\[3pt] 5 &= -5 + b \\[3pt] b &= 10 \end{align*}

Therefore, the equation of the line is \[ y = -1.25x + 10. \]

Finally, we substitute $y =3.75$ into the equation above and solve for $x{:}$ \begin{align*} y & = -1.25x + 10\\[3pt] 3.75 & = -1.25x + 10\\[3pt] 1.25x & = 6.25\\[3pt] x & =5 \end{align*}

Therefore, according to this model, the student spends approximately $5$ hours studying.

Note: The point where $y=3.75$ is not shown on our trend line. Therefore, our result may be unreliable.

question.text:
The scatter plot above shows the population of a town recorded at certain times between the years $2000$ and $2020.$ Assuming this trend continues, estimate the year in which the population will be approximately $40\,000.$

Hint: Assume the trend is linear and that the trend line passes through the points $(2,56)$ and $(18,48).$
question.explanation:
First, using the hint, let's draw an approximate trend line for our scatter plot.

The trend line passes through $(x_1,y_1)=(2,56)$ and $(x_2,y_2)=(18,48).$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form

\[ y=mx+b. \]

First, we find the slope $m$ of the line as follows:

\begin{align*} m &= \dfrac {y_2 - y_1} {x_2 - x_1} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {48 - 56}{18 - 2} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {-8}{16} \\[5pt] &= -0.5 \end{align*}

Substituting $m=-0.5$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

\[ y = -0.5 x + b. \]

We now need to calculate the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can do this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(2,56)\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} y &= -0.5 x + b \\[3pt] 56 &= -0.5(2) + b \\[3pt] 56 &= -1 + b \\[3pt] 57 &= b \\[3pt] b &= 57 \end{align*}

Therefore, the equation of the line is

\[ y = -0.5x + 57. \]

Finally, we substitute $y=40$ into the equation above and solve for $x{:}$

\begin{align*} y &= -0.5x+57 \\[3pt] 40 &= -0.5x+57 \\[3pt] 0.5x+40 &= 57 \\[3pt] 0.5x &= 17 \\[3pt] x &= 34 \end{align*}

Therefore, according to this model, the population will be $40\,000$ around the year $2000+34 = 2034.$

Note: The point where $y=40$ is not shown on our trend line. Therefore, our result may be unreliable.

question.text:
The scatter plot above gives the correspondence between the variables $x$ and $y$ for some data points. Estimate the value of $x$ when $y = 7.$

Hint: Assume the trend is linear, and that the trend line passes through the points $(1,1)$ and $(5,4).$
question.explanation:
First, using the hint, let's draw an approximate trend line for our scatter plot.

Our trend line passes through $(x_1,y_1) = (1,1)$ and $(x_2,y_2)=(5,4).$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form \[ y=mx+b. \]

First, we calculate the slope $m$ of the line as follows: \begin{align*} m & = \dfrac {y_2 - y_1} {x_2 - x_1} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{4 - 1}{5 - 1} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3}{4} \\[5pt] &= 0.75 \end{align*}

Substituting $m = 0.75$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get \[ y = 0.75 x + b. \]

We now need to calculate the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can do this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(1,1)\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} y &= 0.75 x + b \\[3pt] 1 &= 0.75(1) + b \\[3pt] 1 &= 0.75 + b \\[3pt] b &= 0.25 \end{align*}

Therefore, the equation of the line is \[ y = 0.75x + 0.25. \]

Finally, we substitute $y = 7$ into the equation above and solve for $x {:}$ \begin{align*} y & = 0.75x + 0.25\\[3pt] 7 & = 0.75x + 0.25 \\[3pt] 6.75 & = 0.75x \\[3pt] x & = 9 \end{align*}

Therefore, according to this model, when $y=7$ we have $x \approx 9.$

Note: The point where $y=7$ is not shown on our trend line. Therefore, our result may be unreliable.

question.text:
The scatter plot above gives the correspondence between the variables $x$ and $y$ for some data points. Estimate the value of $y$ when $x=23.$

Hint: Assume the trend is linear, and that the trend line passes through the points $(11,8)$ and $(15,7).$
question.explanation:
First, using the hint, let's draw an approximate trend line for our scatter plot.

Our trend line passes through $(x_1,y_1) = (11,8)$ and $(x_2,y_2)=(15,7).$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form \[ y=mx+b. \]

First, we calculate the slope $m$ of the line as follows: \begin{align*} m & = \dfrac {y_2 - y_1} {x_2 - x_1} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{7 - 8}{15 - 11} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{(-1)}{4} \\[5pt] &= -0.25 \end{align*}

Substituting $m = -0.25$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get \[ y = -0.25 x + b. \]

We now need to calculate the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can do this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(11,8)\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} y &= -0.25 x + b \\[3pt] 8 &= -0.25(11) + b \\[3pt] 8 &= -2.75 + b \\[3pt] b &= 10.75 \end{align*}

Therefore, the equation of the line is \[ y = -0.25x + 10.75. \]

Finally, we substitute $x = 23$ into the equation above, which gives \begin{align*} y &= -0.25x + 10.75 \\[3pt] & = -0.25(23) + 10.75 \\[3pt] &= -5.75 + 10.75 \\[3pt] &= 5. \end{align*}

Therefore, according to this model, when $x=23$ we have $y \approx 5.$

Note: The point where $x=23$ is not shown on our trend line. Therefore, our result may be unreliable.
